# PrimeGapsBridge — the network's admissibility is PrimeGapsLib's

**Generated file — do not edit.** Regenerated by `python scripts/graph.py`.

**Status:** proof drafted, not yet built

The network's admissibility (fewer occupied positions than the wheel size, at every wheel) is the same as PrimeGapsLib's (some residue class missed, at every prime). So PrimeGapsLib's Lean results on admissible sets, including infinitely many prime gaps of at most 246 assuming Bombieri-Vinogradov, apply to the network's admissible patterns unchanged.

## Claims

<a id="admissible_iff_primegaps"></a>
### `admissible_iff_primegaps`

An offset pattern is admissible in the network's sense exactly when it is admissible in PrimeGapsLib's sense.

```lean
/-- **The two definitions agree.** An offset pattern is admissible in the
network's sense (fewer occupied positions than the wheel size, at every wheel)
exactly when it is admissible in PrimeGapsLib's sense (some residue class
missed, at every prime). -/
def admissible_iff_primegaps : Prop :=
  ∀ T : Finset Nat, is_admissible T ↔ primegaps_admissible T
```
